### Recommendation: Controlled Soil-Flushing Protocol

Implement a staged, controlled flushing program to move excess soluble nitrogen below the active root zone and restore a more balanced rooting environment.

- Confirm adequate drainage and establish baseline soil nitrate and EC levels.
- Apply irrigation in measured cycles to promote downward movement while minimizing ponding, runoff, and root-zone saturation.
- Collect post-flush soil samples at multiple depths to verify nitrate reduction through the root profile.
- Repeat only as indicated by monitoring results; avoid additional nitrogen inputs until target levels are restored.
- Resume standard irrigation and fertility management gradually, using root-zone data to guide timing.

**Success criteria:** Reduced root-zone nitrate/EC, stabilization of plant condition, and renewed taproot extension in follow-up minirhizotron observations.
